question: How many tonnes of pizza do people in Chicago eat on an average day in 2026?

target.what: Total mass of pizza consumed by people in Chicago (city of Chicago, Illinois) on an average day in calendar year 2026, counting all pizza eaten by residents and visitors within the city, including restaurant/takeout/delivery pizza and any pizza prepared at home from purchased or homemade pizza, meas
target.cadence: Annual average daily flow; no official series exists
target.caveats: Ambiguous scope: (a) pizza eaten within Chicago boundaries by anyone (residents + visitors + commuters) vs (b) pizza eaten by Chicago residents anywhere; working interpretation is (a) consumption occurring within the city, since 'people in Chicago' most naturally means people present in Chicago. Als

candidates.hypothesis: Chicago foodservice pizza sales (USD) divided by average price per pizza/unit and converted to mass via average pizza weight gives foodservice pizza mass; foodservice is expected to be the dominant share (~70-85%) of total pizza consumption. Transfer assumption: city-level pizza sales can be approximated by national per-capita pizza sales scaled to Chicago population, or by Chicago-specific restaurant sales data.
candidates.data_to_find: US pizza restaurant industry annual sales (e.g., from industry associations or market research summaries) for 2024-2026; Chicago/Cook County pizza restaurant sales or number of pizzerias; average price per pizza and average pizza weight (grams) in US foodservice. Minimum evidence: national pizza sales total, Chicago population, average pizza mass per dollar or per transaction.

assumptions.name: Mean pizza mass consumed per pizza-eating occasion (grams)
assumptions.rationale: USDA per-consumer pizza energy of 538 kcal (children) and 744 kcal (adults) (p141, p142) at 220-370 kcal per slice (p139, p140) implies roughly 2-3 slices; at ~100-130 kcal/100 g for cheese pizza that is ~200-350 g. 250 g central with a band covering thin vs deep-dish and child vs adult.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to a daily pizza-consumer prevalence rate to convert occasions to mass; assumes one eating occasion per consumer-day, consistent with NHANES 'intake day' framing.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that Chicago consumers eat materially more slices per occasion (e.g., deep-dish pies at 400+ g/serving) or that multiple pizza occasions per consumer-day are common.

assumptions.name: Chicago pizza-culture prevalence multiplier vs US average
assumptions.rationale: Chicago's deep-dish and tavern-style pizza culture plausibly raises daily pizza prevalence modestly above the 11% US average (p1/p130), but no Chicago-specific dietary data exist; a 1.0-1.4 band brackets 'no premium' to a strong local premium.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to scale the national 11% daily prevalence to Chicago residents.
assumptions.falsified_by: Chicago-specific food-intake survey showing prevalence at or below the national 11%.

assumptions.name: Average daily present population / resident population ratio for Chicago
assumptions.rationale: Census daytime population (p71) vs resident base implies a ~1.07 commuter uplift; adding tourists (56.8M visitors, p67/p164, at ~2-3 nights each) adds a few percent more. Net ~1.10 with a 1.03-1.20 band.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to resident-based consumption to capture pizza eaten by commuters and visitors within city boundaries (target scope a).
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that visitors/commuters eat pizza at much lower rates, or a much larger tourist-night total than assumed.

assumptions.name: Average pizza mass per foodservice order (grams)
assumptions.rationale: A typical order is ~1 medium/large pie (8 slices at ~110 g = ~880 g) or equivalent; deep-dish pies are heavier. 900 g central with 600-1400 g band.
assumptions.applies_when: Used with pizzeria count and daily orders to estimate foodservice pizza mass.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that Chicago orders average multiple pies or that single slices dominate order mix.

assumptions.name: Effective active-pizzeria fraction of listed Chicago pizza restaurants
assumptions.rationale: Business-listing counts (p24, 1,987) include chains, ghost kitchens, and closed units; the true count of operating pizzerias selling meaningful daily volume is lower. 0.75 central with a wide band.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to the listed pizzeria count to get active pizzerias contributing to daily output.
assumptions.falsified_by: A verified registry of active Chicago pizzerias showing near-100% of listings operating.

assumptions.name: Chicago share of US frozen pizza retail sales (per-capita parity)
assumptions.rationale: Chicago's ~2.73M residents are ~0.82% of the US population; assuming per-capita frozen pizza purchases at national parity gives ~0.82% of the $7.3B US frozen pizza market (p58). Band reflects possible local premium/discount.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to allocate national frozen pizza retail dollars to Chicago households.
assumptions.falsified_by: Chicago-specific retail scanner data showing materially different per-capita frozen pizza spend.

assumptions.name: Retail price per kg of frozen pizza (USD/kg)
assumptions.rationale: Frozen pizza retails roughly $4-8 per 400-600 g pie, i.e. ~$7-13/kg; $9/kg central with a band covering private-label to premium.
assumptions.applies_when: Converts Chicago frozen pizza retail dollars to mass.
assumptions.falsified_by: Scanner data showing average frozen pizza price per kg well outside $6.5-13.

assumptions.name: Average pizza mass per foodservice dollar (kg per USD)
assumptions.rationale: At ~$20 per order (p54, p55) and ~900 g per order (a4), mass per dollar is ~0.045 kg/USD; band covers ticket and pie-size variation. Used to convert Chicago foodservice pizza dollars to mass.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to Chicago-attributable foodservice pizza revenue to get foodservice pizza mass.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that Chicago pizza prices per kg differ materially from the ~$22/kg implied here.

assumptions.name: Chicago share of US population (for allocating national pizza totals)
assumptions.rationale: Chicago's ~2.73M residents (p9) against a US population of roughly 335M gives ~0.82%. Used as the allocation share for national pizza revenue and retail totals; band reflects uncertainty in the US denominator and small population drift to 2026.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to scale national US pizza totals (foodservice revenue, frozen retail sales) to Chicago.
assumptions.falsified_by: A materially different US population base or evidence that Chicago's per-capita pizza spend deviates strongly from national parity.

assumptions.name: Non-frozen at-home pizza mass as a fraction of frozen retail pizza mass
assumptions.rationale: USDA source shares show 26% of pizza from grocery stores (p136) versus 56% from restaurants; frozen pizza is the bulk of grocery pizza but refrigerated/fresh and homemade add to it. A ratio of 0.6 (band 0.3-1.2) covers the non-frozen at-home component relative to frozen retail mass.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to gross up the frozen-retail mass to total at-home pizza mass in the channel-sum method.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that fresh/refrigerated and homemade pizza are a much larger or much smaller share of at-home pizza than assumed.

previous_assumptions.rationale: USDA gives 538 kcal (children) and 744 kcal (adults) mean pizza energy per consumer-occasion (p141, p142) and 220-370 kcal per slice (p139, p140), implying ~2-3 slices. At a typical ~100-130 kcal/100g for cheese pizza, that is roughly 200-350 g; 250 g is the central value with a wide band covering thin vs deep-dish and child vs adult.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Applied to a daily pizza-consumer prevalence rate to convert occasions to mass; assumes one eating occasion per consumer-day, consistent with NHANES 'intake day' framing.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that Chicago consumers eat materially more slices per occasion (e.g., deep-dish pies at 400+ g/serving) or that multiple pizza occasions per consumer-day are common.

previous_assumptions.name: Chicago pizza-culture prevalence multiplier vs US average
previous_assumptions.rationale: Chicago's deep-dish and tavern-style pizza culture plausibly raises daily pizza prevalence modestly above the 11% US average (p1/p130), but no Chicago-specific dietary data exist; a 1.0-1.4 band brackets 'no premium' to a strong local premium.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Used to scale the national 11% daily prevalence to Chicago residents.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Chicago-specific food-intake survey showing prevalence at or below the national 11%.

previous_assumptions.name: Average daily present population / resident population ratio for Chicago
previous_assumptions.rationale: Census daytime population (p71) vs resident base implies a ~1.07 commuter uplift; adding tourists (56.8M visitors, p67/p164, at ~2-3 nights each) adds a few percent more. Net ~1.10 with a 1.03-1.20 band.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Applied to resident-based consumption to capture pizza eaten by commuters and visitors within city boundaries (target scope a).
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that visitors/commuters eat pizza at much lower rates, or a much larger tourist-night total than assumed.

previous_assumptions.name: Average pizza mass per foodservice order (grams)
previous_assumptions.rationale: A typical order is ~1 medium/large pie (8 slices at ~110 g = ~880 g) or equivalent; deep-dish pies are heavier. 900 g central with 600-1400 g band.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Used with pizzeria count and daily orders to estimate foodservice pizza mass.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that Chicago orders average multiple pies or that single slices dominate order mix.

previous_assumptions.name: Effective active-pizzeria fraction of listed Chicago pizza restaurants
previous_assumptions.rationale: Business-listing counts (p24, 1,987) include chains, ghost kitchens, and closed units; the true count of operating pizzerias selling meaningful daily volume is lower. 0.75 central with a wide band.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Applied to the listed pizzeria count to get active pizzerias contributing to daily output.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: A verified registry of active Chicago pizzerias showing near-100% of listings operating.

previous_assumptions.name: Chicago share of US frozen pizza retail sales (per-capita parity)
previous_assumptions.rationale: Chicago's ~2.73M residents are ~0.82% of the US population; assuming per-capita frozen pizza purchases at national parity gives ~0.82% of the $7.3B US frozen pizza market (p58). Band reflects possible local premium/discount.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Used to allocate national frozen pizza retail dollars to Chicago households.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Chicago-specific retail scanner data showing materially different per-capita frozen pizza spend.

previous_assumptions.name: Retail price per kg of frozen pizza (USD/kg)
previous_assumptions.rationale: Frozen pizza retails roughly $4-8 per 400-600 g pie, i.e. ~$7-13/kg; $9/kg central with a band covering private-label to premium.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Converts Chicago frozen pizza retail dollars to mass.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Scanner data showing average frozen pizza price per kg well outside $6.5-13.

previous_assumptions.name: Average pizza mass per foodservice dollar (kg per USD)
previous_assumptions.rationale: At ~$20 per order (p54, p55) and ~900 g per order (a4), mass per dollar is ~0.045 kg/USD; band covers ticket and pie-size variation. Used to convert Chicago foodservice pizza dollars to mass.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: Applied to Chicago-attributable foodservice pizza revenue to get foodservice pizza mass.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that Chicago pizza prices per kg differ materially from the ~$22/kg implied here.

kept.name: Mean pizza mass consumed per pizza-eating occasion (grams)
kept.rationale: USDA per-consumer pizza energy of 538 kcal (children) and 744 kcal (adults) (p141, p142) at 220-370 kcal per slice (p139, p140) implies roughly 2-3 slices; at ~100-130 kcal/100 g for cheese pizza that is ~200-350 g. 250 g central with a band covering thin vs deep-dish and child vs adult.
kept.applies_when: Applied to a daily pizza-consumer prevalence rate to convert occasions to mass; assumes one eating occasion per consumer-day, consistent with NHANES 'intake day' framing.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that Chicago consumers eat materially more slices per occasion (e.g., deep-dish pies at 400+ g/serving) or that multiple pizza occasions per consumer-day are common.

kept.name: Chicago pizza-culture prevalence multiplier vs US average
kept.rationale: Chicago's deep-dish and tavern-style pizza culture plausibly raises daily pizza prevalence modestly above the 11% US average (p1/p130), but no Chicago-specific dietary data exist; a 1.0-1.4 band brackets 'no premium' to a strong local premium.
kept.applies_when: Used to scale the national 11% daily prevalence to Chicago residents.
kept.falsified_by: Chicago-specific food-intake survey showing prevalence at or below the national 11%.

kept.name: Average daily present population / resident population ratio for Chicago
kept.rationale: Census daytime population (p71) vs resident base implies a ~1.07 commuter uplift; adding tourists (56.8M visitors, p67/p164, at ~2-3 nights each) adds a few percent more. Net ~1.10 with a 1.03-1.20 band.
kept.applies_when: Applied to resident-based consumption to capture pizza eaten by commuters and visitors within city boundaries (target scope a).
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that visitors/commuters eat pizza at much lower rates, or a much larger tourist-night total than assumed.

kept.name: Average pizza mass per foodservice order (grams)
kept.rationale: A typical order is ~1 medium/large pie (8 slices at ~110 g = ~880 g) or equivalent; deep-dish pies are heavier. 900 g central with 600-1400 g band.
kept.applies_when: Used with pizzeria count and daily orders to estimate foodservice pizza mass.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that Chicago orders average multiple pies or that single slices dominate order mix.

kept.name: Effective active-pizzeria fraction of listed Chicago pizza restaurants
kept.rationale: Business-listing counts (p24, 1,987) include chains, ghost kitchens, and closed units; the true count of operating pizzerias selling meaningful daily volume is lower. 0.75 central with a wide band.
kept.applies_when: Applied to the listed pizzeria count to get active pizzerias contributing to daily output.
kept.falsified_by: A verified registry of active Chicago pizzerias showing near-100% of listings operating.

kept.name: Chicago share of US frozen pizza retail sales (per-capita parity)
kept.rationale: Chicago's ~2.73M residents are ~0.82% of the US population; assuming per-capita frozen pizza purchases at national parity gives ~0.82% of the $7.3B US frozen pizza market (p58). Band reflects possible local premium/discount.
kept.applies_when: Used to allocate national frozen pizza retail dollars to Chicago households.
kept.falsified_by: Chicago-specific retail scanner data showing materially different per-capita frozen pizza spend.

kept.name: Retail price per kg of frozen pizza (USD/kg)
kept.rationale: Frozen pizza retails roughly $4-8 per 400-600 g pie, i.e. ~$7-13/kg; $9/kg central with a band covering private-label to premium.
kept.applies_when: Converts Chicago frozen pizza retail dollars to mass.
kept.falsified_by: Scanner data showing average frozen pizza price per kg well outside $6.5-13.

kept.name: Average pizza mass per foodservice dollar (kg per USD)
kept.rationale: At ~$20 per order (p54, p55) and ~900 g per order (a4), mass per dollar is ~0.045 kg/USD; band covers ticket and pie-size variation. Used to convert Chicago foodservice pizza dollars to mass.
kept.applies_when: Applied to Chicago-attributable foodservice pizza revenue to get foodservice pizza mass.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that Chicago pizza prices per kg differ materially from the ~$22/kg implied here.

rejected.name: Chicago share of US population (for allocating national pizza totals)
rejected.rationale: Chicago's ~2.73M residents (p9) against a US population of roughly 335M gives ~0.82%. Used as the allocation share for national pizza revenue and retail totals; band reflects uncertainty in the US denominator and small population drift to 2026.
rejected.applies_when: Used to scale national US pizza totals (foodservice revenue, frozen retail sales) to Chicago.
rejected.falsified_by: A materially different US population base or evidence that Chicago's per-capita pizza spend deviates strongly from national parity.

rejected.name: Non-frozen at-home pizza mass as a fraction of frozen retail pizza mass
rejected.rationale: USDA source shares show 26% of pizza from grocery stores (p136) versus 56% from restaurants; frozen pizza is the bulk of grocery pizza but refrigerated/fresh and homemade add to it. A ratio of 0.6 (band 0.3-1.2) covers the non-frozen at-home component relative to frozen retail mass.
rejected.applies_when: Used to gross up the frozen-retail mass to total at-home pizza mass in the channel-sum method.
rejected.falsified_by: Evidence that fresh/refrigerated and homemade pizza are a much larger or much smaller share of at-home pizza than assumed.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
